links.outcome: Belief stability of correct diagnoses under escalating multi-turn pressure across nine LLMs
links.effect: High initial diagnostic capability did not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.
links.quote: Across nine frontier large language models (LLMs), we find a clear dissociation between medical knowledge and robustness: high initial diagnostic capability does not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.

links.outcome: Gap between medical benchmark accuracy and belief robustness in clinical dialogue
links.effect: Despite strong medical benchmark accuracy, LLMs showed severe multi-turn sycophancy, abandoning initially correct diagnoses under escalating pressure.
links.quote: Despite strong medical benchmark accuracy, LLMs can exhibit severe multi-turn sycophancy in clinical dialogue, abandoning initial correct diagnosis under escalating pressure.

unlisted_practices: Role-Based Epistemic Defense (RBED) inference-time prompting to resist sycophancy
Resilience-oriented fine-tuning (R-FT) to reduce belief change under pressure

screen.practice: inference-time role-based epistemic defense prompt guardrail
screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating LLM epistemic resilience/sycophancy in clinical dialogue under pressure using a benchmark framework, testing an inference-time prompt defense (RBED) and fine-tuning.
